info.title: Agentic Search API
info.description:
Agentic Search is AVA's open-source web retrieval service for AI agents, derived from Stract. The [source offer](/.well-known/ava-search-source) identifies this build's AGPL-3.0-only source. Read the [crawler policy](/.well-known/ava-search-crawler) for identity, access rules and pending founder approvals. Every API response includes its source URL in the Source-Offer header.

Remember to always give proper attributions to the sources you use from the search results.

post.description: Given a partial query string, returns a list of suggested completions that the user might be typing. Each suggestion is returned with two forms: - `raw`: The complete suggestion text - `highlighted`: The suggestion broken into fragments, with the matching prefix unhighlighted and the completion portion highlighted For example, given the prefix query "shor", a suggestion might be: - raw: "shortest path algorithm" - highlighted: ["shor", "test path algorithm"] The suggestions are ranked by relevance and limited to a reasonable number of results. All returned suggestions will have the original query as a case-insensitive prefix.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The prefix query to generate suggestions for

200.description: suggestions for what the user might be typing

post.description:
A completed website response may include spellCorrection, an escaped display-only offer.
It is absent without a correction, is never executed, and always has applied: false.
The original query, selected stages and retrieval results are preserved.

The main search endpoint that powers Stract's web search functionality. It performs a full-text search
across all pages in the index and returns the most relevant results.

The endpoint supports the [optic syntax](https://github.com/StractOrg/sample-optics/blob/main/quickstart.optic)
that can be used to customize the search results and perform advanced filtering.
If the query matches the bang prefix `!`, the result will be a redirect to the bang target.
For example, `!w cats` redirects to Wikipedia's page on cats.

Results are paginated and can be flattened into a simpler format if desired. The response includes
rich metadata like snippets, titles, and ranking signal scores (when enabled).

200.description: Search results with first-producing stages. Multistage numHits is an approximate largest-stage estimate, not an exact union; later pages remain strict.

post.description:
The sidebar endpoint returns a sidebar that matches the query. The sidebar is a UI component
that provides additional information or navigation options related to the query at the top of the search results.

The endpoint returns an empty response if no relevant sidebar content is found for the given query.
When content is found, it returns a structured response containing the sidebar data needed
to render the component.

For example, a query for "Aristotle" might return a sidebar with biographical information,
key philosophical concepts, and links to related ancient Greek philosophers.

200.description: The sidebar if one matches the query

post.description:
The spellcheck endpoint checks a query string for spelling errors and returns a corrected version if needed.
The correction is returned with highlighting to show what was changed.

For example, given the query "hwllo eorld", it might return "hello world" with "hello" and "world"
highlighted to show the corrections.

The corrections aim to preserve the user's intent while fixing obvious mistakes.

The correction dictionary has been trained on common words and phrases on the web, so it might make mistakes itself.

200.description: The corrected string or an empty response if there is no correction to be made.

post.description:
The widget endpoint returns a widget that matches the query. Widgets are special UI components
that provide direct answers or interactive functionality for certain types of queries at the top of the search results.
A widget could for example be a calculator for math expressions, or a thesaurus for word definitions.

The endpoint returns an empty response if no widget matches the given query. When a widget does match,
it returns a structured response containing the widget type and its specific data needed to render it.

200.description: The resulting widget if one matches the query

post.description:
Returns the incoming edges (backlinks) for a particular host. For example, if site A links to site B,
then site A would appear in the ingoing edges for site B.

The results are limited to a reasonable number of the most important inbound edges.
Edges are considered more important if they come from authoritative sites.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The host to get edges for

200.description: Incoming edges for a particular host

post.description:
Returns the outgoing edges (forwardlinks) for a particular host. For example, if site A links to site B,
then site B would appear in the outgoing edges for site A.

The results are limited to a reasonable number of the most important outbound edges.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The host to get edges for

200.description: Outgoing edges for a particular host

post.description:
Returns a list of hosts similar to the given hosts. The similarity between hosts is calculated
based on how similar their inbound edges are - hosts that tend to be linked to by the
same other hosts are considered more similar.

For example, two news websites might be considered similar because they are both frequently
linked to from social media sites, news aggregators, and blogs discussing current events.

Returns the incoming edges (backlinks) for a particular page. For example, if page A links to page B,
then page A would appear in the ingoing edges for page B.

The results are limited to a reasonable number of the most important inbound edges.
Edges are considered more important if they come from authoritative sites.

200.description: Incoming edges for a particular page

post.description:
Returns the outgoing edges (forwardlinks) for a particular page. For example, if page A links to page B,

The results are limited to a reasonable number of the most important outbound edges.

PlanMode.description: Why a request uses one or several eligible stages.

PlanTerm.description: A source-level term; literals remain query data and are serialized with JSON escaping.

kind.description: Closed parser meaning, never an arbitrary schema field supplied by a client.

occur.description: Mandatory, excluded, threshold or optional preference occurrence.

text.description: Canonical literal or operand text, retaining its case and punctuation.

weight.description: Declared weight, exactly one or two; unrelated to learned ranking coefficients.

numHitsScope.description: Whether numHits describes one stage or an approximate multistage estimate.

stages.description: Only completed stages actually sent, in execution order; never skipped placeholders.

QueryServiceError.description: Sanitized failures; none carry request strings, addresses or dependency errors.

oneOf.description: Completed bare-bang request without a redirect target.

SearchErrorCode.description: Closed union of safe client-input, service and bare-bang error codes.

SearchErrorDetail.description: Fixed error detail without query text or infrastructure data.

message.description: Fixed safe message associated with the code.

SearchErrorResponse.description: Search-route JSON error envelope used for HTTP 400, 404, 413 and 503.

error.description: The typed failure; no successful result fields accompany it.

query.description: The query string to search for

filters.description: Filters the similar hosts to only include those that match the given filters

hosts.description: The hosts to find similar hosts for

topN.description: The number of similar hosts to return

SourceOffer.description: Public source identity of the running build, with no machine or user information.

licence.description: SPDX identifier of the service's source offer.

revision.description: Full lowercase Git SHA-1, or unknown.

revision_source.description: Observable provenance: git, environment or unknown.

source_url.description: Public pinned source URL, or repository discovery URL for unknown builds.

applied.description: Always false: this offered correction did not participate in retrieval.

SpellCorrectionOffer.description:
Optional website-search correction whose raw and highlighted text is escaped for display.
The correction is never executed and applied is always false; the separate spelling
endpoint retains its existing unescaped DTO semantics. Deserialize rejects applied true.
Both serde and bincode decoders enforce this invariant. Bincode support is required
by the parent WebsitesResult derive; no service message carries its spelling offer.

query.description: The query string to possibly correct

StageId.description: Ordered, finite stage identifiers; public rendering uses lowercase strings.

StageProvenance.description: One completed stage, measured around fan-out, ranking and retrieval at the API.

addedCount.description: Slots actually added to the accumulated output.

elapsedMs.description: Complete stage elapsed wall time, rounded down to whole milliseconds.

hitCount.description: Sum of successful shard match counts before trimming/deduplication.

minimumShouldMatch.description: Distinct content-atom vote threshold, null outside relaxed/core.

producedResults.description: Exactly returnedCount > 0; duplicate-only stages may add no slots.

renderedQuery.description: Complete actual lexical compilation plus named digests for applied request filters.

returnedCount.description: Retrieved stage page size before cross-stage deduplication, at most requested count.

rewrittenQuery.description: Readable source query, never reparsed for execution.

terms.description: Selected source-ordered atoms, with optional phrases after their first constituent.

TermKind.description: Closed source-level term kinds, excluding schema field identifiers.

TermOccur.description: An atom's role in the selected candidate or preference query.

oneOf.description: Completed stages and first-producing attribution; omitted for internal legacy callers.
Optional escaped display correction, absent without an offer; never executed, applied always false.

query.description: The query string to search for
